## #1713 [Code Health] hbg: Graph recording path still goes through the ring — the N→1 / no-ring / no-upload benefit applies only to replays

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1713
- Created: 2026-08-06T07:04:57Z
- Updated: 2026-08-10T06:14:54Z
- Closed: 2026-08-10T06:14:54Z

### Body

## Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

## Component

Orchestration

## Description

On a cache miss (recording), a Graph's internal tasks are submitted as ordinary tasks: they occupy **N ring task-window slots**, take **N ring-heap allocations**, and **upload N payloads**, while being recorded. Only cache hits (replays) get the "one outer GRAPH slot, internal nodes off the ring, nothing uploaded" benefit.

Because the Definition cache is per-run (starts empty each run), the recording layer is re-paid **every run** — for a repeated decoder loop, the first layer of each run pays the full N-slot ring cost while later layers replay. For a 3-layer decode this is "layer 0 fully through the ring; layers 1–2 saved."

## Location

- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/orchestration/pto_orchestration_api.h` — `rt_submit_graph_impl` (a cache miss runs the function normally through the ordinary submit path).
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/orchestrator_core/pto_orchestrator.cpp` — recording path (internal tasks submitted as real ring tasks on a miss).

## Proposed Fix

Build the first invocation directly into the separate host-owned execution block and execute it as a Graph, so the ring holds only the outer GRAPH task even on the recording run. This requires switching the recording layer from "execute-while-record (internal tasks through the ring)" to "record the layout first, then execute as a Graph." Feasible under the Step-1 fixed-structure contract: the topology is fully determined without executing the tasks, and the consolidated `required_heap` size is known once recording finishes.

## Priority

Medium — a per-run one-time recording cost, re-paid every run in a repeated decode loop.

## Additional Context

Sub-issue of #1706. Deliberately deferred out of PR #1444; filed for follow-up.

## #1715 [Feature] hbg: Port Graph Execution to a5

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1715
- Created: 2026-08-06T07:28:36Z
- Updated: 2026-08-10T09:14:07Z
- Closed: 2026-08-10T09:14:07Z

### Body

### Summary

Port Graph Execution to `src/a5/runtime/host_build_graph/`. It landed for a2a3 in #1444 and
was never brought over, and it is now the **only** capability a5 HBG lacks relative to a2a3.

A file-by-file comparison of the two trees shows five a2a3-only files, all of them Graph
Execution:

```text
runtime/graph_cache.h
runtime/graph_execution.h
runtime/graph_host_state.h
runtime/scheduler/graph_execution.cpp
docs/GRAPH_EXECUTION.md
```

Its plumbing also accounts for most of the content divergence in the files both trees share,
so the port is wider than those five files:

| Shared file | What a5 is missing |
| ----------- | ------------------ |
| `orchestration/pto_orchestration_api.h` | `rt_submit_graph` and the `GRAPH_KEY` identity overload |
| `runtime/orchestrator_core/pto_orchestrator.cpp` | recording (`GraphRecording`, `GraphRecordedNode`, tensor-source classification), Definition compaction, boundary-contract validation, cache-hit submission |
| `runtime/pto_runtime2_types.h` | the `TaskKind` enum (`KERNEL` / `DUMMY` / `GRAPH` / `GRAPH_NODE`) and the slot's `task_kind` field — a5 carries `uint8_t _async_pad` in that byte |
| `runtime/scheduler/pto_scheduler.h`, `scheduler_dispatch.cpp` | `TaskCompletionOutcome` / `stream_tasks_completed`, so a graph-internal node contributes 0 to the host-visible completion count instead of 1; `graph_prepare_queue` / `graph_ready_queue` and their bounded per-loop expansion |
| `runtime/pto_runtime2.h`, `host/runtime_maker.cpp` | `active_callable_hash` (the Definition cache key) and the exact-size POD submission-image upload path |
| `runtime/scheduler/scheduler_cold_path.cpp` | graph slot reporting in the cold-path dump |

Scene coverage comes with it: `tests/st/a2a3/host_build_graph/graph_execution/` has four
scenes (AIV fanin/fanout DAG, Qwen-style decoder-layer DAG, three-slot multi-block MIX/SPMD,
manual Qwen3-14B three-layer decode) and a5 has none.

### Motivation / Use Case

Graph Execution is the mechanism that makes host orchestration affordable for repetitive
graphs: the first invocation records the DAG, later invocations submit one `GRAPH` task whose
internal nodes the device Scheduler expands from a saved Definition, consuming no ring slots
and costing no re-submission. Without it, every repeated subgraph on a5 — an LLM decoder
layer submitted per layer and per token being the motivating shape — is rebuilt on the host
in full, every run.

That makes this a gap in the runtime's purpose, not just in its feature list. The
`host_build_graph` vision in #1706 rests on amortizing the host build cost, so an a5 HBG
without Graph Execution cannot reach the same destination as a2a3.

It is also the standing rule in #1706 that HBG is one runtime with two arch trees, and that a
deliberate divergence needs a stated hardware reason. There is no hardware reason here — the
absence is lag from #1444 not being mirrored.

### Proposed API / Behavior

No new API. The a5 orchestration surface, wire format, and device-side behavior should match
a2a3's exactly, so `docs/GRAPH_EXECUTION.md` describes both after the port (either copied to
the a5 tree or made arch-neutral and shared).

Arch-specific points to verify rather than copy blindly:

- **Core geometry.** a5 is `RUNTIME_MAX_WORKER 108` (36 AIC + 72 AIV) against a2a3's 72
  (24 AIC + 48 AIV). Check the MIX placement bitset, whose flattened offset is `cluster * 3`,
  and any node/tensor ceiling derived from core counts.
- **Completion mailbox ABI.** `DeferredCompletionEntry` is 32 bytes on a5 against 24 on a2a3.
  Confirm graph-internal node completion routes through the same endpoint on a5.
- **AICPU thread topology.** a5 resolves a different `aicpu_thread_num`; the 3S+1P split and
  the graph prepare/ready queues are per-thread structures.
- **DFX.** The `Graph Execution` and `graph_prepare` swimlane lanes need the a5 collectors,
  and a5's PMU path is `pmu_aicpu_complete_record` where a2a3 uses `pmu_aicpu_record_task`.

Bring the four `graph_execution` scenes over as part of the same change, so the port is
verified rather than merely compiled.

### Alternatives Considered

**Leave Graph Execution a2a3-only.** Rejected: it would be a permanent capability split with
no hardware justification, which is exactly what #1706 asks contributors not to create
silently. If a5 is ever to be excluded on purpose, that needs its own decision and a stated
reason.

**Wait for Graph Execution step 2 to settle first, then port once.** Reasonable in principle,
but step 2 is open-ended (#1712, #1713 and the rest of the "Current unsupported cases" list),
so this would defer a5 indefinitely. Porting step 1 now and carrying step-2 work in both trees
per the usual same-commit rule keeps the trees converged.

### Additional Context

Parent tracking issue: #1706 (`host_build_graph` — intent, vision & change tracking).

Related: #1444 (the a2a3 implementation), #1712 and #1713 (Graph Execution step-2 work on
a2a3), #1582 (the analogous a2a3-vs-a5 divergence reconciliation for
`tensormap_and_ringbuffer`).

Whatever a2a3 Graph Execution looks like when this is picked up is what should be ported —
this issue is not pinned to #1444's exact state.

## #1716 [Code Health] hbg: Port host-overhead reduction (#1659) to a5

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1716
- Created: 2026-08-06T07:36:25Z
- Updated: 2026-08-11T09:23:23Z
- Closed: 2026-08-11T09:23:23Z

### Body

### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

Host Runtime

### Description

#1659 landed on **a2a3 `host_build_graph` only**. It cuts HBG per-dispatch host `bind`
by up to ~99% (paged_attention 402.7 ms → ~7.8 ms) by stopping three kinds of wasted
work that scale with ring capacity instead of the actual task count:

1. **Bounded SM H2D upload** — the shared-memory mirror is sized to ring capacity (task
   window, tens of thousands of slots) but a run only writes `[0, total_tasks)`, and the
   device boots scheduler-only and reads no slot past `total_tasks`. Each segment
   (`descriptors` / `payloads` / `slot_states` / `completion_flags`) is now uploaded
   bounded to `[0, total_tasks)`.
2. **Init-on-write, no window-wide reset** — per-slot `reset_for_reuse()` + completion-flag
   clear moved out of the boot-time whole-window loop into `orch::prepare_task` as each
   slot is claimed. The unclaimed tail is neither initialized nor uploaded nor read.
3. **Skip the host-only orchestrator block** — the arena's `fanin_seen_epoch` /
   `scope_tasks` / TensorMap block (~8.5 MB) is host-only dep-computation scratch the
   AICPU scheduler never reads, so it is sliced out of the arena H2D entirely.

Plus the guardrails that shipped with it: a named `PTO2_ERROR_READY_QUEUE_OVERFLOW`
latched from `push_ready_routed`, an `always_assert(orch_start <= orch_end)` layout guard,
and a poison cpput test pinning the "every device-read field is written at submit" contract.

**a5 `host_build_graph` still carries the full pre-#1659 code** (verified on `main` @
`29b119d1`): the boot-time blanket `reset_for_reuse()` loop and whole-array completion-flag
zero, full `sm_size` SM upload and full `arena_size` arena upload, and no
`READY_QUEUE_OVERFLOW`. HBG is one runtime with two arch trees kept in sync (see #1706),
so a5 pays the same host overhead until this ports over.

### Location

a5 sites still on the old code (mirroring the a2a3 files #1659 changed):

- `src/a5/runtime/host_build_graph/host/runtime_maker.cpp` — full `copy_to_device(device_sm, host_sm, sm_size)` (~:535) and full `copy_to_device(runtime_arena_dev, ..., layout.arena_size)` (~:877); no `total_tasks` bounding, no orch-block slice, no layout assert.
- `src/a5/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/shared/pto_shared_memory.cpp:189,195` — boot-time whole-window `reset_for_reuse()` loop + "Zero the whole per-ring array once".
- `src/a5/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/orchestrator_core/pto_orchestrator.cpp` — `prepare_task` lacks the init-on-write reset + completion-flag clear.
- `src/a5/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/scheduler/pto_scheduler.h` — `push_ready_routed` does not check the push return / latch overflow.
- `src/a5/runtime/host_build_graph/common/pto_runtime_status.h` — no `PTO2_ERROR_READY_QUEUE_OVERFLOW`.
- `src/a5/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/{pto_runtime2_types.h,pto_shared_memory.h,shared/pto_runtime2_init.cpp}` — the four `reset_for_reuse` doc/comment sites still describe the old "once at init" behavior.
- `src/a5/runtime/host_build_graph/docs/RUNTIME_LOGIC.md` — no §3.1 Bounded H2D Upload section.
- `tests/ut/cpp/` — no a5 equivalent of `test_hbg_submit_poison.cpp`.

### Proposed Fix

Port the #1659 diff onto the a5 tree file-for-file (per rule codestyle §10: finish each
identifier across arch siblings). One caveat to resolve during the port:

- On a2a3 the **ready queues ship in full** (not bounded) specifically because #1444 graph
  execution expands a GRAPH task into on-device nodes that push past the host task count.
  Graph execution is **not yet on a5** (#1715). To keep the two trees identical and avoid a
  a5-local divergence that #1715 would then have to unwind, mirror a2a3 exactly — ship the
  queues whole. Do not bound them on a5 just because a5 lacks graph execution today.

Source PR: #1659. Sibling a5 port precedent: #1715. Tracking: #1706.

### Priority

Medium (minor risk, should fix in next few releases)

## #1717 [Feature] hbg: Overlap device launch with host orchestration to hide per-run launch latency

- State: open
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1717
- Created: 2026-08-06T07:44:33Z
- Updated: 2026-08-10T06:31:35Z
- Closed: 

### Body

## Summary

After removing intra-run O/S streaming (PR #1444), `host_build_graph` runs strictly serial per run: the host builds the complete task image (O), uploads it, then launches the resident Scheduler (S). The device launch is a per-run cost on the critical path between O-done and S-start, not overlapped with anything. This optimization overlaps the device launch with the host-orchestration build so the launch latency is hidden.

## Motivation / Use Case

Host orchestration (O) builds the task image on a host thread writing host-side shadow SM — it does not touch the device until upload. The device launch (device bring-up + launching the AICPU Scheduler kernel against an empty image) is independent of O's build and can run concurrently. Overlapping them hides the per-run launch latency behind O.

Run-to-run pipelining (prepared-successor) already hides O + launch for steady-state runs (run N+1's preparation overlaps run N's device execution), so the main beneficiary is the **cold start / first run** — the one case pipelining cannot cover — plus any run where O is short relative to launch.

## Proposed API / Behavior

- Launch the device (empty image) on one path while the host-orchestration build runs concurrently on another (O already runs on a separate thread).
- Have the Scheduler wait on a single "orchestration done + total_tasks" startup handshake before it begins dispatching the complete image. O→S stays serial at the scheduling level; only the launch is overlapped.
- The device startup wait may block / sleep-poll — startup handshakes are exempt from the no-sleep-on-dispatch-path rule (`.claude/rules/codestyle.md` §5).

This is deliberately NOT the removed streaming design: a single end-of-orchestration handshake, no incremental publish, no `orchestrator_done`-vs-`current_task_index` streaming read (and therefore none of that ordering hazard).

## Scope — a2a3 AND a5 together

`src/a5/runtime/host_build_graph/` now also exists, and the launch path is shared platform code (`src/common/platform/**/host/c_api_shared.cpp`, `src/{a2a3,a5}/platform/onboard/host/device_runner.cpp`). Both arches' HBG do host orchestration and benefit identically, so this should land for a2a3 and a5 in the same change rather than a2a3-first.

## Alternatives Considered

- Leave it serial and rely solely on run-to-run pipelining — misses cold-start / first-run launch latency.
- A persistent Scheduler daemon (launch once at init, loop across runs) — larger architectural change (the Scheduler currently exits at EOS per run); out of scope here.

## Additional Context

Deferred out of PR #1444, which removed the entangled intra-run streaming. Related to #1706 (a2a3 HBG tracking) but cross-arch (a2a3 + a5).

## #1719 [Code Health] hbg: Delete the zero-caller fanin_satisfied()

- State: open
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1719
- Created: 2026-08-06T08:45:45Z
- Updated: 2026-08-06T08:50:31Z
- Closed: 

### Body

### Category

Dead Code / Unused Dependencies

### Component

AICPU Scheduler

### Description

`SchedulerContext::fanin_satisfied()` has no callers anywhere in the
`host_build_graph` tree, on either architecture, and has had none since the day it
landed.

It is the boolean sibling of `classify_fanin_state()`. Both walk the same loop over
`payload->fanin_local_ids[]` checking `ring.is_completion_flag_set()`; the only
difference is the return value:

```cpp
bool fanin_satisfied(const PTO2TaskSlotState *s) const {
    for (int32_t i = 0; i < p.fanin_count; i++)
        if (!ring.is_completion_flag_set(p.fanin_local_ids[i])) return false;
    return true;
}

int classify_fanin_state(const PTO2TaskSlotState *s) const {
    for (int32_t i = 0; i < p.fanin_count; i++)
        if (!ring.is_completion_flag_set(p.fanin_local_ids[i])) return i;
    return -1;
}
```

`classify_fanin_state` strictly subsumes it — `fanin_satisfied(s)` is exactly
`classify_fanin_state(s) == -1`. The readiness path needs the *index*, not the
boolean, because a consumer whose scan finds an unmet producer registers on **that
producer's** wake list. Both call sites that matter (boot classification and the
wake-list drain) therefore call `classify_fanin_state`; the boolean form was never
reached.

This is not a leftover from the `tensormap_and_ringbuffer` port — T&R has no such
function on either arch, because its wiring model decides readiness by counting
`fanin_count` down rather than scanning a fanin array. Both functions were
introduced together by #1435 when the polling completion scheduler replaced the
wiring subsystem, and the boolean one arrived with zero callers:
`git show b39d45ba^:…/pto_scheduler.h` contains no occurrence of the name, and
`b39d45ba` contains exactly one — the definition.

Two comments describe the design in terms of the unused function, which is why it
reads as load-bearing. They must move to `classify_fanin_state` in the same change,
or the next reader re-derives this whole investigation.

Impact is small — one unused inline function and two misleading comments — but the
cost of keeping it is that every reader of the readiness path has to work out which
of two identical-looking scans is the live one.

### Location

```markdown
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/scheduler/pto_scheduler.h:512` — the definition
- `src/a5/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/scheduler/pto_scheduler.h:499` — the a5 copy, also zero-caller
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/pto_runtime2_types.h:258` — comment naming it as a reader of `completion_flags`
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/orchestrator_core/pto_orchestrator.cpp:859` — comment describing boot classify as "fanin_satisfied -> push_ready_routed, else register_wake"
- `src/a5/...` — both comments exist in the a5 tree at the same places
```

### Proposed Fix

Delete `fanin_satisfied()` from both arch trees and reword the two comments to name
`classify_fanin_state` and its `-1` / first-unmet-index contract. No behavior change;
nothing to verify beyond a build and the existing `host_build_graph` scene suites.

Land both trees in the same commit, per the one-implementation rule in #1706.

### Priority

Low (no impact today, good to fix eventually)

## #1720 [Code Health] hbg: Retire last_task_alive and the dead mid-run reclamation path

- State: open
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1720
- Created: 2026-08-06T08:45:49Z
- Updated: 2026-08-14T05:55:32Z
- Closed: 

### Body

### Category

Dead Code / Unused Dependencies

### Component

Ring Buffer

### Description

`host_build_graph` still carries the complete mid-run reclamation subsystem it
inherited from `tensormap_and_ringbuffer`, driven by a shared-memory field that
**nothing in HBG ever writes**.

`PTO2RingFlowControl::last_task_alive` is defined as the orchestrator↔scheduler
back-pressure channel — its own comment says *"Cache Line 1: Written by Scheduler,
Read by Orchestrator (for back-pressure)"*. In T&R the on-device orchestrator and the
schedulers share the ring, and the scheduler advancing this field is what releases
task slots and heap bytes for reuse.

HBG is whole-graph-resident and reclaims nothing during a run, so the scheduler
deliberately does not advance it — `pto_scheduler.h:26`: *"there is no on-device slot
reclaim (whole-graph-resident), so `last_task_alive` is not advanced here."* Outside
`init()` there is no writer in the tree. It is pinned at 0 for the whole run.

The host orchestrator nevertheless reads it on every submit and drives an entire
chain of code that can only ever be a no-op:

| Site | What it does with a permanently-zero value |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `pto_orchestrator.cpp:1169`, `:1494` | `sync_tensormap(task_id, 0)` → `sync_validity(0)` and a periodic `cleanup_retired(0, 0)` that can never free an entry |
| `pto_tensormap.h:668` | `is_entry_valid` compares `producer_local >= last_task_alive_cached`, i.e. `>= 0` — unconditionally true |
| `pto_orchestrator.cpp:1191-1192` | `dep_local_task_id < dep_last_task_alive`, the "producer already retired, no fanin wiring needed" shortcut — unreachable |
| `pto_ring_buffer.h:159` | `// Spin: wait for scheduler to advance last_task_alive` — a spin whose exit condition can never be met |
| `pto_ring_buffer.h:272` | `last_alive_seen_` / `update_heap_tail()`, the heap-side half of the same reclaim |
| `pto_runtime2_init.cpp:268` | passes `last_alive_dev` into `PTO2TaskAllocator::init` |

Two things make this worth removing rather than tolerating.

**It costs work on the hot build path.** Every submit pays `sync_tensormap`, an epoch
compare, and a periodic `cleanup_retired` walk that provably frees nothing. Host build
time is on HBG's critical path, so this is not free.

**It produces a misleading diagnosis on the failure that matters most.** When the graph
does not fit, the allocator enters the spin above, waits for a reclaim that can never
arrive, and the §4.1 wall-clock backstop eventually latches
`FATAL: Task Allocator Deadlock - Heap Exhausted!`. There is no deadlock: the graph
simply exceeds the configured task window or heap. Anyone triaging that message starts
by looking for a dependency cycle.

HBG already has the signal that actually matters for consumer retirement, and it is a
different field: `completed_watermark`, which the scheduler advances and the host's
`wait_for_consumers` gates on (`watermark >= producer.last_consumer_local_id`). Nothing
about removing `last_task_alive` touches it.

Note what must **not** be removed: the TensorMap lookup itself is how HBG derives
dependencies, and the heap allocator's *allocation* cursor is how packed buffers get
addresses. Only the retirement/reclaim halves are dead.

### Location

```markdown
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/pto_shared_memory.h:55` — the field, plus `static_assert(sizeof(PTO2RingFlowControl) == 128)` that its removal changes
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/pto_shared_memory.h:297` — `ring_last_task_alive_addr`
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/pto_ring_buffer.h:159`, `:272` — the never-satisfiable spin and `last_alive_seen_` / `update_heap_tail`
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/pto_tensormap.h:378`, `:394-405`, `:492`, `:582-590`, `:668` — `last_task_alive_cached`, `reclaim_retired_all`, `sync_validity`, `cleanup_retired`, `is_entry_valid`
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/shared/pto_tensormap.cpp:211-220` — `sync_tensormap` and `PTO2_TENSORMAP_CLEANUP_INTERVAL`
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/orchestrator_core/pto_orchestrator.cpp:1041`, `:1169`, `:1191-1192`, `:1494` — the reads and the retired-producer shortcut
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/shared/pto_runtime2_init.cpp:92`, `:268` — init and the allocator constructor argument
- `src/a5/runtime/host_build_graph/` — the same sites exist in the a5 tree
```

### Proposed Fix

Remove the field and every consumer listed above, in both arch trees in one commit.

**This changes one behavior and the change is the point:** a graph that does not fit
the configured task window, heap, fanin capacity or TensorMap pool must fail
immediately with a capacity error naming the exhausted resource and the requested vs.
available amount, instead of spinning until the wall-clock backstop reports a
"deadlock". Update the §4.1 text in `RUNTIME_LOGIC.md` accordingly — the representative
allocator output quoted there changes.

`PTO2_ERROR_TENSORMAP_OVERFLOW`'s description (*"tensormap entry pool wedged
(last_task_alive not advancing)"*) also needs rewording, since after this change there
is no such thing as a pool that could have been unwedged by reclaim.

Sequencing: this touches `pto_runtime2_init.cpp` and `scheduler_dispatch.cpp` regions
that the multi-ring collapse also touches. Land this before that one, or rebase.

### Priority

Medium (minor risk, should fix in next few releases)

## #1721 [Code Health] hbg: Collapse the degenerate multi-ring machinery (PTO2_MAX_RING_DEPTH == 1)

- State: open
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1721
- Created: 2026-08-06T08:45:54Z
- Updated: 2026-08-06T08:50:39Z
- Closed: 

### Body

### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

Ring Buffer

### Description

`host_build_graph` fixes `PTO2_MAX_RING_DEPTH` at **1**
(`pto_runtime2_types.h:81`), but the code around it is still written as if the depth
were variable — 73 occurrences across 10 files of single-iteration loops,
one-element arrays, threaded `ring_id` parameters, and validations that cannot fail.

The mechanism it came from is real, but it does not apply here. T&R sets the depth to
**4** and splits TaskRing, HeapRing and DepPool into four independent instances so a
nested scope gets isolated ring space and cannot be starved by an outer scope's
un-reclaimed tasks. It is fundamentally a *reclaim*-isolation device. HBG is
whole-graph-resident and reclaims nothing during a run, so there is nothing to
isolate, and the depth was set to 1 accordingly.

What remains:

| Shape | Example |
| ----- | ------- |
| Single-iteration loops | `for (int r = 0; r < PTO2_MAX_RING_DEPTH; r++)` in `pto_runtime2_init.cpp`, `pto_shared_memory.cpp`, `scheduler_cold_path.cpp`, `pto_scheduler.cpp`, `pto_orchestrator.cpp` |
| One-element arrays | `heap_sizes[PTO2_MAX_RING_DEPTH]`, `task_window_sizes[PTO2_MAX_RING_DEPTH]`, the per-ring SM header section |
| Threaded parameter | `PTO2RingFlowControl::validate(handle, int32_t ring_id)` |
| Unreachable validation | `prod_ring >= PTO2_MAX_RING_DEPTH` in `PTO2FaninBuilder::mark_seen`, whose own next line reads *"Single-ring hbg: prod_ring is always 0."* |

`runtime_maker.cpp` carries 22 of the 73 occurrences and already contains
`static_assert(PTO2_MAX_RING_DEPTH == 1, "relocate_host_orch_image assumes a single
ring")` — one path has stopped pretending to be general while the rest still is. That
mixed state is the actual defect: a reader cannot tell from the code whether multi-ring
is a supported configuration of HBG or a fiction.

### Location

```markdown
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/pto_runtime2_types.h:81` — `#define PTO2_MAX_RING_DEPTH 1`
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/host/runtime_maker.cpp` — 22 occurrences, incl. the `static_assert` at `:363`
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/shared/pto_shared_memory.cpp` — 20 occurrences
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/shared/pto_runtime2_init.cpp` — 11 occurrences
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/pto_shared_memory.h` — 6, incl. `validate(handle, ring_id)` at `:69`
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/pto_runtime2.h` — 5
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/{pto_runtime2_types.h,pto_ring_buffer.h}`, `runtime/scheduler/{scheduler_cold_path.cpp,pto_scheduler.cpp}`, `runtime/orchestrator_core/pto_orchestrator.cpp` — the remainder
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/orchestrator_core/pto_orchestrator.cpp:735` — `prod_ring >= PTO2_MAX_RING_DEPTH` in `mark_seen`
- `src/a5/runtime/host_build_graph/` — the same surface exists in the a5 tree
```

### Proposed Fix

**Decide the direction first — this issue is not a mechanical delete.**

Option 1, collapse: drop the loops and one-element arrays, remove `ring_id` from
internal signatures, and delete the unreachable validations. The code says what it
does; re-introducing depth > 1 later means re-deriving the loops.

Option 2, keep the shape: leave the structure so HBG stays diffable against T&R, and
only delete what is provably unreachable (the `mark_seen` guard, validations behind the
existing `static_assert`). Cheaper, but leaves the mixed state largely intact.

**One carve-out applies to either option: do not change the `PTO2TaskId` encoding.**
`(ring_id << 32) | local_id` looks like an obvious simplification — the upper half is
always zero in HBG — but it is a host↔device wire field parsed by runtime-agnostic DFX
tooling: `deps_viewer.py:129,149,157` and `swimlane_converter.py:90,105,115,129,144,381,409`
all decode `(tid >> 32)` as the ring id, and `swimlane_converter.py:129` branches on it
being a specific value. Those tools serve T&R too, where ring ids 0–3 are real. Changing
the encoding for HBG alone breaks a shared parser, so the id layout stays as it is
regardless of what happens to the loops.

Whichever option is chosen, land both arch trees in the same commit per #1706, and land
this **after** the `last_task_alive` removal — this one touches `pto_runtime2_init.cpp`,
`pto_shared_memory.cpp` and `runtime_maker.cpp` broadly enough to conflict with almost
anything else in flight.

### Priority

Low (no impact today, good to fix eventually)

## #1727 [Feature] hbg: Add benchmark cases and harness/skill support (default stays tmr)

- State: open
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1727
- Created: 2026-08-07T03:06:20Z
- Updated: 2026-08-10T08:14:38Z
- Closed: 

### Body

### Summary

`host_build_graph` has no benchmark path at all. The whole benchmark story — the
`tools/benchmark_rounds.sh` harness, the `benchmark` skill, and the example corpus —
is `tensormap_and_ringbuffer`-only. Add HBG support across all three, keeping T&R the
default and making HBG selectable.

Three separate gaps, in increasing order of difficulty:

**1. The harness refuses the runtime.** `benchmark_rounds.sh` dispatches on
`case "$RUNTIME"` and the only arm is `tensormap_and_ringbuffer`; anything else exits
with *"ERROR: unknown runtime … Use tensormap_and_ringbuffer"*
(`tools/benchmark_rounds.sh:165-172`). The workload list is a single T&R-specific pair
of arrays, `TMR_EXAMPLE_CASES` / `TMR_EXAMPLE_ORDER` (`:37-57`).

**2. There are almost no HBG benchmark cases.** In the merged tree, not one of the six
T&R benchmark workloads has an HBG counterpart under `tests/st/a2a3/host_build_graph/` or
`examples/a2a3/host_build_graph/`. Two open PRs close part of this — see
[the PR section below](#part-of-the-corpus-already-exists-in-open-prs--merge-them-do-not-re-author):

| T&R benchmark case | HBG counterpart |
| ------------------ | --------------- |
| `alternating_matmul_add` (Case1) | — |
| `benchmark_bgemm` (Case0) | — |
| `paged_attention_unroll` (Case1,Case2) | — |
| `paged_attention_unroll_manual_scope` (Case1,Case2) | — |
| `batch_paged_attention` (Case1) | — |
| `qwen3_14b_decode` (StressBatch16Seq3500) | open PR #1666 |

The nearest available HBG scenes are `bgemm` (case `default`), `matmul` (`default`) and
`paged_attention` (`Case1`, `Case2`) — related workloads, but not the same ones, so they
cannot be read as a cross-runtime comparison.

**3. Four of the five reported metrics do not exist on HBG.** The harness reports Host /
Device / Effective / Orch / Sched, and all but Host are derived from `AicpuPhase`
markers rendered by `simpler_setup.tools.strace_timing --rounds-table`. **The HBG tree
emits zero `AicpuPhase` markers** — `grep -c AicpuPhase src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/`
returns nothing, against `OrchWindow` / `SchedWindow` / `Preamble` / `ConfigValidate` /
`ArenaWire` / `SmReset` in the T&R tree. Only Host works, because the host-side STRACE
span lives in `src/common/`.

This one is not a wiring problem, it is a semantic one: HBG's orchestrator runs **on the
host**, so a `device_wall.orch` span is not merely missing, it is meaningless. The phases
worth timing in HBG are different — host graph build, pointer relocation, the single
H2D, boot classification, dispatch — plus the split between the S threads and the P
resolution thread, and record-vs-replay for Graph Execution.

### Motivation / Use Case

**A merged performance PR has no harness behind it.** #1659 (*"HBG: up to 99% host-side
overhead reduction"*) reports paged_attention host `bind` going 402.7 ms → ~7.8 ms. That
was measured ad hoc. Nobody can re-run it, confirm it, or notice when it regresses, and
#1716 is about porting that same work to a5 — which will need the same measurement to
show it landed.

**HBG's central claim is unverified.** The runtime's thesis in #1706 is that host
orchestration is affordable because the build cost is amortized — by Graph replay
(#1444) and by prepared-successor pipelining. Both are performance arguments with no
performance evidence. Bucket 6 of #1706 exists precisely for this, and every other
performance sub-issue (#1713 on the recording path still paying full ring cost, #1717 on
overlapping device launch with orchestration) is a claim this harness would settle.

**T&R-vs-HBG has never been measured on the same graph.** That comparison is the input
to the "where should HBG land" question in #1706 — whether host orchestration plus Graph
replay beats device orchestration for repetitive, statically-shaped graphs.

### Proposed API / Behavior

**Harness.** Add `HBG_EXAMPLE_CASES` / `HBG_EXAMPLE_ORDER` alongside the T&R arrays and a
second arm in the runtime dispatch. `tensormap_and_ringbuffer` stays the default, so
`./tools/benchmark_rounds.sh` with no `-r` behaves exactly as today; `-r host_build_graph`
selects the HBG corpus.

`--serial-orch-sched` must be rejected for HBG rather than silently accepted: it exists to
serialize a device-side orchestrator against the schedulers, and HBG has none.

**Metrics.** Decide the HBG column set before writing the cases, because it determines what
instrumentation is needed:

- *Option A* — give HBG its own `AicpuPhase` markers for the phases it actually has, and
  report an HBG-shaped table (host build / relocate / H2D / boot classify / dispatch,
  with S-vs-P attribution). Most useful, most work.
- *Option B* — report only what exists today (Host, plus device wall if it can be derived
  without per-phase markers) and state plainly in the output that the Orch/Sched columns
  are T&R-only. Cheap, honest, and unblocks regression tracking on the metric #1659 was
  about (host `bind`).

Either way the table must not print empty or zero columns that look like measurements.

**Cases.** Merge #1666 and #1667 first (see below) — they already supply
`qwen3_14b_decode`, `paged_attention` and `paged_attention_manual_scope` in one-to-one
positions, which covers the workload #1659's claim was measured on and the
repetitive-decode workload Graph Execution targets. Everything still missing is authoring
work that overlaps the coverage gap in #1706 bucket 5, and each new copy must follow the
rule #1666 and #1667 already follow: same tree, same directory name, same case names, so
the HBG and T&R numbers stay directly comparable.

Graph Execution deserves a benchmark axis of its own: same graph with and without replay
is the direct measurement of the amortization claim.

**Skill.** `.claude/skills/benchmark/SKILL.md` §"Runtime Selection" currently lists only
`tensormap_and_ringbuffer (default)`. Add `host_build_graph`, keep the default, and
document what changes about the reported columns when it is selected — a table whose
column meanings silently change per runtime is worse than one that says so. The same
applies to `perf-runtime-device` and `perf-example-device`, which accept a runtime
argument and would otherwise point users at a harness that rejects HBG.

### Part of the corpus already exists in open PRs — merge them, do not re-author

Two open PRs already add HBG copies of T&R examples, and **both place them one-to-one
with their T&R counterparts** — same tree, same directory name, same file layout, only
the runtime directory differs. No separate case-authoring PR is needed for what they
cover; merging them is the work.

| PR | Adds | T&R counterpart | Placement | Cases |
| -- | ---- | --------------- | --------- | ----- |
| #1666 | `examples/a2a3/host_build_graph/qwen3_14b_decode/` | `examples/a2a3/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/qwen3_14b_decode/` | one-to-one | **identical** — all 38, including `StressBatch16Seq3500`, the exact case `TMR_EXAMPLE_CASES` benchmarks |
| #1667 | `examples/a2a3/host_build_graph/paged_attention/` | `examples/a2a3/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/paged_attention/` | one-to-one | 10 of 11 — `Case3` deliberately omitted |
| #1667 | `examples/a2a3/host_build_graph/paged_attention_manual_scope/` | `examples/a2a3/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/paged_attention_manual_scope/` | one-to-one | same 10 of 11 |

The `Case3` omission is justified in #1667's own description and is not an HBG gap: it
is `manual: True` (so it never runs in CI), it uses `head_dim: 256`, and it fails on
**both** runtimes — `max_diff=nan` on HBG and `max_diff=0.1255` on the unmodified T&R
example, with a normal ~16 ms `device_wall` and no allocator fatal. That is a
pre-existing kernel numerics defect above `head_dim > 128`, so copying it would import a
known-failing case. #1667 reports 12/12 passing across both examples on a2a3 with golden
checking.

What this leaves for the benchmark corpus, against the current `TMR_EXAMPLE_CASES`:

| T&R benchmark case | Tree | Covered by |
| ------------------ | ---- | ---------- |
| `qwen3_14b_decode` (`StressBatch16Seq3500`) | `examples/` | **#1666** |
| `alternating_matmul_add` (Case1) | `tests/st/` | still to author |
| `benchmark_bgemm` (Case0) | `examples/` | still to author |
| `paged_attention_unroll` (Case1,Case2) | `tests/st/` | still to author |
| `paged_attention_unroll_manual_scope` (Case1,Case2) | `examples/` | still to author |
| `batch_paged_attention` (Case1) | `tests/st/` | still to author |

`qwen3_14b_decode` is the most valuable single entry, since it is the repetitive-decode
shape Graph Execution is designed for. #1667's two examples are not in
`TMR_EXAMPLE_CASES` today, but they mirror T&R examples exactly, so `HBG_EXAMPLE_CASES`
can include them and the numbers stay directly comparable — the HBG list does not have to
be a name-for-name copy of the T&R list, it has to consist of cases that exist one-to-one
on both sides.

**One conflict to resolve before or with #1667.** `tests/st/a2a3/host_build_graph/paged_attention/`
already exists in the tree, and T&R has no `tests/st/.../paged_attention` at all — its
`paged_attention` lives only under `examples/`. So merging #1667 leaves HBG with two
different `paged_attention` scenes, only one of which corresponds to anything on the T&R
side. They are not the same content: the existing `tests/st` copy is 156 lines with cases
`Case1` / `Case2` / `small1` / `small2`, against #1667's 10 cases using T&R's
`CaseSmall1` / `CaseSmall2` spelling. The `tests/st` copy should be removed in favour of
#1667's, or its continued existence justified — otherwise the one-to-one placement rule is
broken the moment #1667 lands.

### Alternatives Considered

**Keep measuring ad hoc (status quo).** This is what #1659 did. It produced a number
nobody can reproduce and no barrier against regressing it — and the port in #1716 has no
way to demonstrate parity.

**Run the T&R harness unmodified against HBG.** It exits at the runtime dispatch. Even if
that check were simply relaxed, the run would report Orch/Sched/Device columns with no
data behind them, which is worse than refusing: a table of zeros reads as a measurement.

### Additional Context

Parent: #1706 (bucket 6, Benchmark). Related: #1659 (the unreproducible claim), #1716 (a5
port needing the same measurement), #1713 and #1717 (HBG performance claims this harness
would verify), #1712 (Graph step-2 work whose payoff needs measuring).

**Incidental finding while surveying the harness — `--serial-orch-sched` has never
worked.** `benchmark_rounds.sh:249` runs the second pass with `PTO2_SERIAL_ORCH_SCHED=1`,
but the runtime reads `SIMPLER_TMR_SERIAL_ORCH_SCHED_ENABLE`
(`src/{a2a3,a5}/runtime/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/host/runtime_maker.cpp:629`). Nothing
consumes the variable the script sets, so both passes run in the default overlapped mode
and the *"Serial vs Parallel Delta"* table at `:413-416` compares a configuration against
itself. The skill's own text (`SKILL.md:120`) names the correct variable, so the script is
the side that is wrong. This is a separate defect from the HBG work here and should get
its own issue.

## #1734 [Code Health] Derive tmr scheduler thread/core dimensions from platform_config constants instead of magic literals

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1734
- Created: 2026-08-07T07:17:00Z
- Updated: 2026-08-10T03:31:28Z
- Closed: 2026-08-10T03:31:28Z

### Body

### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

AICPU Scheduler

### Description

Several hardware-derived dimensions in the tmr scheduler are written as bare numeric literals even though `platform_config.h` already defines the exact named constant they equal. The literals obscure that a2a3 and a5 share one rule, read as divergences when they are not, and go silently wrong if a platform constant ever changes. This issue covers the three that are the *same* problem — "use the existing platform constant instead of a magic literal" — and should land across both trees in one commit per `.claude/rules/codestyle.md` rule 10.

**G (dummy-drain thread gate).** The Phase 3 dummy-drain gate hardcodes which scheduler threads participate:

- a2a3 `scheduler_dispatch.cpp`: `if (thread_idx < 3)`
- a5 `scheduler_dispatch.cpp`: `if (thread_idx < 4)` (after #1679; currently `thread_idx == 0` on main)

The literal is exactly `PLATFORM_MAX_AICPU_THREADS - 1` (a2a3 MAX=4, a5 MAX=5) — "every scheduler thread except the last". The two literals differ *only* because the platform cap differs. The same `MAX - 1` rule is already a named constant in both trees: `RUNTIME_DEFAULT_READY_QUEUE_SHARDS = PLATFORM_MAX_AICPU_THREADS - 1`.

**M1 (`RUNTIME_MAX_WORKER`).** `scheduler_context.h` hardcodes the max-worker array dimension with a per-tree literal:

- a2a3: `#define RUNTIME_MAX_WORKER 72`
- a5:   `#define RUNTIME_MAX_WORKER 108`

This equals `PLATFORM_MAX_CORES`, which is itself already `PLATFORM_MAX_BLOCKDIM * PLATFORM_CORES_PER_BLOCKDIM` (72 / 108, and the platform header even annotates it `// 72` / `// 108`). A hand-maintained two-tree divergence that a named constant already computes.

**M2 (cores-per-cluster `3`).** The scheduler uses a bare `3` for "cores per cluster" (1 AIC + 2 AIV) where `PLATFORM_CORES_PER_BLOCKDIM == 3` already exists (and is used one line up at `scheduler_types.h:142` in `MAX_CORE_PER_THREAD = MAX_CLUSTERS * PLATFORM_CORES_PER_BLOCKDIM`). Both trees identical.

> **Scope note for M2:** only the *semantic* multiply/divide sites should be swapped — `core_num() { return cluster_count_ * 3; }`, the `cores_total_num_ / 3`, the `% 3 != 0` validity check and its "multiple of 3" error text. The bitmask-layout arithmetic (`bit(i*3)`, `bit(i*3+1)`, `bit(i*3+2)` for AIC/AIV0/AIV1) is self-documenting with its adjacent comment and reads fine as-is; rewriting it inflates the diff for no clarity gain. Leave it, or only touch it if a reviewer prefers.

No behavior change is intended — every derived value equals the current literal on both arches today.

### Location

**G — dummy-drain gate:**
- `src/a2a3/runtime/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/runtime/scheduler/scheduler_dispatch.cpp:1187` — `if (thread_idx < 3)`
- `src/a5/runtime/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/runtime/scheduler/scheduler_dispatch.cpp` — dummy-drain gate (`thread_idx < 4` after #1679)

**M1 — `RUNTIME_MAX_WORKER`:**
- `src/a2a3/runtime/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/runtime/scheduler/scheduler_context.h:29` — `#define RUNTIME_MAX_WORKER 72`
- `src/a5/runtime/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/runtime/scheduler/scheduler_context.h:28` — `#define RUNTIME_MAX_WORKER 108`

**M2 — cores-per-cluster `3` (semantic sites):**
- `src/a5/runtime/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/runtime/scheduler/scheduler_types.h:475` — `core_num() { return cluster_count_ * 3; }` (and a2a3 sibling)
- `src/{a2a3,a5}/runtime/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/runtime/scheduler/scheduler_cold_path.cpp` — `cores_total_num_ / 3`, `% 3 != 0`, `"multiple of 3"` error string

**Reference constants (both trees):**
- `src/{a2a3,a5}/platform/include/common/platform_config.h` — `PLATFORM_MAX_AICPU_THREADS` (4 / 5), `PLATFORM_CORES_PER_BLOCKDIM` (3), `PLATFORM_MAX_CORES = PLATFORM_MAX_BLOCKDIM * PLATFORM_CORES_PER_BLOCKDIM` (72 / 108)
- `src/{a2a3,a5}/runtime/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/runtime/runtime.h` — `RUNTIME_DEFAULT_READY_QUEUE_SHARDS = PLATFORM_MAX_AICPU_THREADS - 1`

### Proposed Fix

Replace each literal with the derived constant, landing a2a3 + a5 in one commit (rule 10) so both trees read identically:

- **G:** `if (thread_idx < PLATFORM_MAX_AICPU_THREADS - 1)` (or reuse `RUNTIME_DEFAULT_READY_QUEUE_SHARDS` for a scheduler-visible name).
- **M1:** default `RUNTIME_MAX_WORKER` to `PLATFORM_MAX_CORES` instead of the per-tree `72` / `108` literal (keep the `#ifndef` override guard).
- **M2:** swap the semantic `* 3` / `/ 3` / `% 3` sites to `PLATFORM_CORES_PER_BLOCKDIM`; leave the `bit(i*3+k)` layout arithmetic as-is.

Verify afterward: `grep -n "thread_idx < 3\|thread_idx < 4" scheduler_dispatch.cpp` and the `RUNTIME_MAX_WORKER 72\|108` / bare `* 3` semantic sites return zero hits. Best sequenced after #1679 (A3) merges so the a5 gate already reads `thread_idx < 4`.

Deliberately **out of scope** (tracked/left for a separate issue): the 4-copy TU-local `PTO2_DEFERRED_RELEASE_CAP = 256` (a dedup-to-shared-header problem, not a platform-derivation one).

Related: #1582 (a2a3 vs a5 tmr reconciliation), #1679 (A3 dummy-drain parallelization).

### Priority

Low (no impact today, good to fix eventually)

### Body

### Category

Robustness (potential edge-case failure)

### Component

AICPU Scheduler

### Description

PR #1733 intentionally keeps the A5 Graph Execution change as a direct port of the existing A2/A3 implementation. Cross-architecture hardening discovered during review is deferred so it can be designed, implemented, and validated for A2/A3 and A5 together.

The follow-up should cover:

- report Graph ready/prepare queue insertion failures instead of dropping work or spinning indefinitely;
- distinguish all resolved async completions from host-visible stream-task completions for watchdog progress;
- route Graph fatal paths through one idempotent scheduler shutdown helper;
- report invalid Graph-node completion state instead of allowing a later timeout;
- validate uploaded Graph wire-image lengths and embedded Definition bounds;
- bounds-check retained tensor patches on affine replay;
- make activation-gate retry semantics explicitly one-shot; and
- add matching regression coverage for both architectures.

A reviewed prototype is preserved at [c3e6b60a](https://github.com/zmnobug/simpler/commit/c3e6b60a48dd62d0b5351aea0209a66a640982b5).

Related: #1706, #1710, #1715, PR #1733.

- src/a5/runtime/host_build_graph/host/runtime_maker.cpp

- tests/ut/cpp/{a2a3,a5}/test_graph_cache.cpp

### Proposed Fix

Implement the hardening as one cross-architecture change after PR #1733 lands. Keep the A2/A3 and A5 scheduler behavior aligned, add architecture-parallel unit tests, rebuild both runtimes, and run both HBG simulation suites plus available onboard CI.

## #1737 [Code Health] Deduplicate HBG Graph Execution across A2/A3 and A5

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1737
- Created: 2026-08-07T09:16:49Z
- Updated: 2026-08-17T03:25:28Z
- Closed: 2026-08-17T03:25:28Z

### Body

### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

Host Runtime

### Description

PR #1733 intentionally keeps separate A2/A3 and A5 Graph Execution implementations so the A5 change remains a direct, reviewable port. The architecture-neutral cache, wire ABI, host recording state, materialization logic, documentation, and unit-test structure are therefore duplicated for now.

Once both architecture implementations have stabilized, the duplicated logic should be extracted without mixing that refactor into the initial A5 enablement.

A prototype of the shared layout is preserved at [c3e6b60a](https://github.com/zmnobug/simpler/commit/c3e6b60a48dd62d0b5351aea0209a66a640982b5).

Related: #1715, #1706, #1582, PR #1733.

## #1740 [Code Health] Pod L4 examples are enumerated by hand instead of collected by the ST framework

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1740
- Created: 2026-08-08T00:28:57Z
- Updated: 2026-08-10T08:59:06Z
- Closed: 2026-08-10T08:59:06Z

### Body

### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

Tests

### Description

The pod job registers each L4 two-machine example as its own hand-written workflow step, while every other worker example is collected by pytest and scheduled by the ST framework in `conftest.py`. The asymmetry is not cosmetic: it means the L4 examples get none of what that framework provides, and adding one costs four edits to `_st-pod.yml` instead of zero.

**How the L2/L3 examples are wired.** Each one ships a thin `test_*.py` next to its `main.py` that declares its resource needs as markers and delegates to `main.run(...)`, e.g. `examples/workers/l3/allreduce/test_allreduce.py`:

```python
@pytest.mark.platforms(["a2a3sim", "a2a3"])
@pytest.mark.runtime("tensormap_and_ringbuffer")
@pytest.mark.device_count(2)
def test_allreduce(st_platform, st_device_ids):
    rc = run([int(d) for d in st_device_ids], platform=st_platform)
    assert rc == 0
```

`conftest.py::_collect_resource_jobs` picks these up as `kind="standalone"` jobs (any non-class function carrying `device_count` + `runtime`), bin-packs them with the L3 `SceneTestCase` classes through `parallel_scheduler.run_jobs`, and hands each one its devices via the `st_device_ids` fixture. One `pytest examples tests/st` invocation in `_st-npu-a2a3.yml` collects all of them; `--platform` filtering, device allocation, marker-based skipping and quarantine (`-m "not sdma"`) all come for free.

Counting `test_*.py` under `examples/workers/`: **l2 = 5, l3 = 10, l4 = 0**. The three L4 examples have only `main.py` + `run_parent.sh`.

**What the L4 examples get instead.** Three near-identical 8-line steps in `_st-pod.yml`, each with a hand-assigned `id:`, plus a matching line in the `Report pod example results` shell script, because `continue-on-error: true` rewrites a failed step's `conclusion` to success and only `outcome` carries the truth.

**Consequences:**

1. **Registration is manual and duplicated in two places.** Adding a fourth example means: a new step, a unique `id:`, a new `env-prefix`, and a new line in the summary script. Forgetting the summary line is silent — the example runs, fails, and the job still reports green, which is the exact failure mode `.claude/rules/ci-change-detection.md` §7 warns about ("a gating bug shows up as a green check").
2. **No platform declaration.** The L2/L3 examples state `@pytest.mark.platforms([...])`. The L4 examples encode their target platform as a shell default inside `run_parent.sh` (`SIMPLER_..._PLATFORM:=a2a3`), so nothing prevents the pod job from invoking one against a platform it was never written for, and nothing skips it when the pod machines don't match.
3. **`conftest.py` has no concept of a second machine at all.** Grepping it for `remote` / `peer` / `node_count` / `pod` returns nothing. So this is a genuine framework gap, not an example that forgot to opt in — the `st_device_ids` fixture allocates local devices from a local pool, and there is no fixture that could hand a test the peer's endpoint.
4. **The two suites can drift.** A `conftest.py` change to device allocation, platform filtering or quarantine applies to 15 examples and silently skips 3.

### Location

```markdown
- `.github/workflows/_st-pod.yml` — the three enumerated `pod-run-example` steps and the `Report pod example results` script that mirrors them
- `conftest.py::_collect_resource_jobs` — collects `kind="standalone"` jobs from `device_count` + `runtime` markers; no multi-machine notion
- `conftest.py::st_platform`, `conftest.py::st_device_ids` — allocate from a local device pool only
- `examples/workers/l3/allreduce/test_allreduce.py` — the pattern the L4 examples do not follow
- `examples/workers/l4/{vector_add,global_tload,compute_then_tload}_mixed_l3/` — `main.py` + `run_parent.sh`, no `test_*.py`
```

### Proposed Fix

The blocker is that a pod test needs the peer endpoint, and no fixture can currently supply it. Two options, in increasing scope:

**(a) Collapse the enumeration without touching `conftest.py`.** Keep the shell driver, but make the step list data instead of copy-paste — a matrix over `(example, env-prefix, parent-script)`, or a single step looping over the examples and accumulating failures. This removes the summary-script duplication (consequence 1) and nothing else. Small, and worth doing regardless.

**(b) Give the framework a pod fixture and let pytest collect the L4 examples too.** Add a `peer_endpoint` fixture that reads the pod `.env` values the workflow already resolves (`POD_REMOTE_HOST`, `POD_L3_DAEMON_PORT`, `POD_REMOTE_DEVICES`) and skips when they're absent, plus a marker for "needs a peer machine" so `_collect_resource_jobs` can route it. Then each L4 example gets the same thin `test_*.py` its L2/L3 siblings have, and `_st-pod.yml` shrinks to one pytest invocation with a peer-selecting marker. This addresses all four consequences, and starting the daemon stays in the action (it must outlive the step).

Note that (b) subsumes (a) but is meaningfully larger, since the daemon lifecycle currently lives in `.github/actions/pod-run-example` and would need to be reachable from a fixture or hoisted to a once-per-job step. Suggest doing (a) now and treating (b) as the real fix.

Whichever path: the summary-script mirroring should go away, since a registration that can be half-completed and still report green is the part most likely to bite.

### Priority

Medium (minor risk, should fix in next few releases)

## #1742 [Code Health] simpler_finalize_run's launched semantics change (#1694) undocumented in any commit message

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1742
- Created: 2026-08-08T00:56:14Z
- Updated: 2026-08-08T02:43:24Z
- Closed: 2026-08-08T02:43:24Z

### Body

### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

Host Runtime

### Description

`launched` in `simpler_finalize_run` was silently redefined from `phase != NativeRunPhase::Prepared` to `state->active_execution != nullptr` by PR #1694 ("Refactor: run native progress on the child loop", `4f417732`). Neither PR #1694's nor PR #1725's ("Attach the device before drain and retire the dead dep_gen capture API", `0d202898`) commit message mentions `launched`, `Prepared`, or `active_execution` — verified by reading both commit messages in full.

The new definition looks correct: a `NotStarted` failure never touched a stream, so it should take the `-1` / `set_gm_sm_ptr(nullptr)` path rather than being treated as launched. This isn't a report of a functional bug — it's that the invariant behind `launched` has never been stated anywhere (no code comment, no commit message), so a future regression on this path has no explanation to `git bisect` back to, and the next person to touch this function has to re-derive the invariant from scratch.

Originally surfaced during PR #1694 review as one of four non-blocking follow-ups; PR #1725 closed the other three (dep_gen dead API removal, two restored tests, `catch (...) {}` diagnostics) but did not touch this one.

### Location

- `src/common/platform/onboard/host/c_api_shared.cpp:856` (`simpler_finalize_run`)
- `src/common/platform/sim/host/c_api_shared.cpp:762` (same function, sim variant)

### Proposed Fix

Add a comment at the `launched` definition stating the present-tense invariant it encodes — e.g. that `launched` means "the native run reached the point of owning an `active_execution` and therefore needs `drain_execution`", as opposed to the pre-#1694 phase-based definition. No behavior change is being requested; this is purely recording the existing invariant so it survives the next refactor.

### Priority

Low (no impact today, good to fix eventually)

## #1764 [Code Health] MailboxState conflates task phase, init, control and directives in one 13-value enum

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1764
- Created: 2026-08-10T09:33:37Z
- Updated: 2026-08-11T03:19:30Z
- Closed: 2026-08-11T03:19:30Z

### Body

### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

Host Runtime

### Description

`MailboxState` is a single 13-value enum that carries **four unrelated kinds of
thing** in one shared-memory word. This is the unfinished half of the
async-preparation pipeline's E2 step: *"let the mailbox express only phase, and
store the preparation disposition separately."* The disposition half shipped in #1650
(`48dc78bf`, as a side effect of unrelated work rather than any E2 PR):
`MailboxPreparationDisposition` (`worker_manager.h:84-88`) got its own frame
offset, its own validation, and a poison path for out-of-enum values. The
phase half did not.

Today's members, grouped by what they actually are (hit counts across `src/` +
`python/`):

| Kind | Members | Uses |
| ---- | ------- | ---- |
| **Task phase** — the only kind E2 wants to keep here | `IDLE=0` · `TASK_READY=1` · `FRAME_STAGED=8` · `TASK_LAUNCHED=9` · `TASK_DONE=2` · `TASK_FAILED=10` | — |
| **Init lifecycle** | `INIT_READY=6` · `INIT_FAILED=7` | 30 · 17 |
| **Control channel** | `CONTROL_REQUEST=4` · `CONTROL_DONE=5` | 12 · 17 |
| **Directives written by the peer** | `SHUTDOWN=3` · `ACTIVATE=11` · `PREPARE_READY=12` | 32 · 10 · 8 |

`ACTIVATE` is not an observed state at all — it is CAS-written *into* the word
as a command (`worker_manager.cpp:724` does `FRAME_STAGED -> ACTIVATE`).

Three consequences, none of which a rename fixes:

**1. The phase values are interleaved, so "is this a phase?" needs a hand-written
set.** They occupy 1, 2, 8, 9, 10, with non-phase values at 3–7, 11, 12. The
resulting predicate is spelled out by hand, e.g. `worker.py:2702`:

```python
live_states = (_TASK_READY, _PREPARE_READY, _ACTIVATE, _FRAME_STAGED, _TASK_LAUNCHED)
```

Two directives mixed with three phases in one tuple — exactly the conflation E2
exists to remove. Every such set must be maintained by hand and can silently
disagree with the next one.

**2. The `TASK_` / `FRAME_` prefixes are load-bearing, not noise.** The step's
target vocabulary is `READY / STAGED / LAUNCHED / DONE / FAILED`; the code needs
the prefixes *only* to disambiguate from `INIT_READY` and `CONTROL_DONE` in the
same enum. So renaming before splitting produces a strictly worse state —
`READY` sitting next to `INIT_READY`. **The rename is a consequence of the
split, not a substitute for it.**

**3. `FRAME_STAGED` already means two different things in one header.**
`MailboxState::FRAME_STAGED = 8` (`:77`) and
`WorkerProgressKind::FRAME_STAGED = 0` (`:291`). Same identifier, same file,
different values.

**The constraint that shapes any fix:** this word is a cross-process wire
contract, not an internal enum. It is a `volatile int32_t` at
`MAILBOX_OFF_STATE` mutated by `mailbox_compare_exchange_state`, in shared
memory between a parent and its forked children — the POD boundary in
`.claude/rules/codestyle.md` §8. And the Python side **re-declares all 13
values by hand** as module constants (`worker.py:310-329`), with no generation
or assertion tying them to the C++ enum.

Therefore: **renaming enumerators is free (compile-time only); renumbering is
not** — an already-running child and a freshly started parent must agree on the
integers. Any fix has to keep the numeric values fixed or ship a synchronized
change on both sides.

Not on the critical path for anything today. Filing it so the scope is on record
rather than being re-estimated as "just a rename" — which is how it was
previously (mis)scoped.

### Location

Verified against `upstream/main@4739cbf4`:

```markdown
- `src/common/hierarchical/worker_manager.h:60-82` — `MailboxState`, the 13-value enum
- `src/common/hierarchical/worker_manager.h:77` — `MailboxState::FRAME_STAGED = 8`
- `src/common/hierarchical/worker_manager.h:290-294` — `WorkerProgressKind`, whose `FRAME_STAGED = 0` (`:291`) collides by name
- `src/common/hierarchical/worker_manager.h:117` — `MAILBOX_OFF_STATE`, the shared-memory offset of the word
- `src/common/hierarchical/worker_manager.cpp:724` — `ACTIVATE` CAS-written as a directive (`FRAME_STAGED -> ACTIVATE`)
- `python/simpler/worker.py:310-329` — all 13 values re-declared by hand, no single source of truth
- `python/simpler/worker.py:2702` — `live_states`, a hand-written set mixing directives with phases
```

### Proposed Fix

**Split by concern while keeping every numeric value unchanged**, so nothing on
the wire moves:

- `MailboxTaskPhase` — `IDLE`, `TASK_READY`, `FRAME_STAGED`, `TASK_LAUNCHED`,
  `TASK_DONE`, `TASK_FAILED`
- `MailboxInitState` — `INIT_READY`, `INIT_FAILED`
- `MailboxControlState` — `CONTROL_REQUEST`, `CONTROL_DONE`
- `MailboxDirective` — `SHUTDOWN`, `ACTIVATE`, `PREPARE_READY`

They continue to share the one word, with value ranges that do not overlap, so
the split is source-level only and no running pair can disagree.

Then, and only then, drop the now-redundant `TASK_` / `FRAME_` prefixes, and
rename `WorkerProgressKind::FRAME_STAGED` or the phase member so the collision
in `worker_manager.h` goes away.

Independently worth doing and cheap: give the Python constants a generation step
or a start-up assertion against the C++ values, so the two cannot drift
silently. That is the part with real (if latent) risk today — a wrong constant
there is a silent cross-process protocol mismatch, not a compile error.

### Priority

Low (no impact today, good to fix eventually)

Related: #1650 (delivered the disposition half) · #1728 and #1739 (E1/E1', the
sibling step, both complete)

## #1768 [CI] st-pod-onboard-a2a3 fails ~half of runs from pod-runner network, not from the change under test

- State: open
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1768
- Created: 2026-08-11T01:29:33Z
- Updated: 2026-08-11T01:29:33Z
- Closed: 

### Body

### Platform

a2a3

### Runtime Variant

Not runtime-specific — the job fails before or independently of any runtime code.

### Description

`st-pod-onboard-a2a3` has failed **4 times across 3 consecutive PRs** in the last
two days, every time from a cause on the pod runner rather than from the change
under test. Each one cleared on a plain re-run.

Filing because the individual failures are each easy to wave off as "flaky", but
they are not one flake — they are **three distinct failure modes with a common
root**: that runner cannot reliably reach GitHub. A job that is re-run to green
four times without anyone recording why is indistinguishable from a job that is
quietly hiding a real regression, which is the situation
[`discipline.md`](../blob/main/.claude/rules/discipline.md) §5 exists to prevent.

| # | PR | Job | Cause |
| - | -- | --- | ----- |
| 1 | #1748 | [93181456452](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/actions/runs/31288343867/job/93181456452) | `finalize_native_run failed with code -100` (SCHEDULER_TIMEOUT) in the forked chip child |
| 2 | #1761 | [93386587323](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/actions/runs/31366488734/job/93386587323) | `actions/upload-artifact` download failed — SSL + 100 s HttpClient timeout, 3 attempts |
| 3 | #1761 | [93406263088](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/actions/runs/31372831310/job/93406263088) | `actions/checkout` **and** `actions/upload-artifact` both failed to download, same SSL/timeout |
| 4 | #1765 | [93426741349](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/actions/runs/31379371085/job/93426741349) | pto-isa auto-clone failed → `OSError: PTO-ISA not available` → wheel build failed |

Failures 2, 3 and 4 never ran a test at all. Failure 4 is the clearest statement
of the root cause:

```
OSError: PTO-ISA not available.
  The managed checkout must live at .../build/pto-isa and match .../pto_isa.pin.
  If auto-clone failed, manually run:
    git clone https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pto-isa.git .../build/pto-isa
ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed.
*** CMake build failed
```

Three of the four are the same underlying problem — `codeload.github.com` and
`github.com` are not reliably reachable from that runner. Failure 1 is different
in kind (a device-side scheduler timeout) and may be unrelated; I am listing it
for completeness rather than claiming it shares the cause.

Corroborating, though from a different machine: over the same period, `git
fetch` / `git push` / `gh api` from the dev box repeatedly failed with
`Failed to connect to github.com port 443`, `OpenSSL SSL_read: unexpected eof
while reading`, and `Empty reply from server`, all resolving on retry. So this
may be a network-path problem broader than the one runner.

### Steps to Reproduce

Open any PR that does not skip `st-pod-onboard-a2a3` and watch the job. It fails
roughly half the time. No property of the change under test is required — failures
2, 3 and 4 were on a **docs-and-comment-only** PR (#1761) and a PR whose only
runtime effect is an import-time assertion (#1765).

### Expected Behavior

Either the job runs the pod tests and reports their result, or it fails for a
reason attributable to the change under test.

### Actual Behavior

The job fails during environment setup — downloading actions, or cloning pto-isa —
and reports red for a change that cannot have caused it. Re-running clears it.

### Git Commit ID

Observed across `b4b89c67` (#1748) through `0fc77f21` (#1765).

### CANN Version

Not applicable — 3 of the 4 failures occur before any device code runs.

### Driver Version

Not applicable.

### Host Platform

Self-hosted pod runner `a2a3pod-1`
(`/data/workspace/ci-runner/hw-native-sys-simpler/a2a3pod-1`).

### Additional Context

Two things worth deciding, neither of which I want to guess at:

1. **Whether the runner's network egress can be fixed or proxied.** If
   `codeload.github.com` is unreachable often enough to fail half of all runs, an
   action cache or a pre-provisioned pto-isa checkout on the runner would remove
   three of these four failure modes outright.
2. **Whether failure 1 (SCHEDULER_TIMEOUT) is the same story.** It is the only one
   that got as far as running a test, and it is the only one that could plausibly
   be a real device-side issue. It has not recurred in the three runs since.

I have been re-running this job to green rather than reporting it, which is the
habit this issue is meant to end.

## #1772 Reduce CI per-job wall time

- State: open
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1772
- Created: 2026-08-11T03:35:43Z
- Updated: 2026-08-11T06:25:16Z
- Closed: 

### Body

### Platform

All / Unknown

### Runtime Variant

All / Unknown

### Summary

Several CI jobs are close to or above 10 minutes. The goal is to reduce the
wall time of each existing job without splitting jobs or changing the current
`pre-commit` gate.

The initial focus is:

- `st-sim-a2a3`
- `st-sim-a5`
- `st-onboard-a2a3`
- `st-onboard-a5`

The solution must support both GitHub-hosted and self-hosted execution. The
self-hosted sim runner also starts from a fresh server for each run, while
Onboard runners have different performance tiers.

### Git Commit ID

04791a72be375b6d9774c07ae280a401651fd3af

### CANN Version

N/A — CI-level optimization across simulation and hardware jobs.

### Driver Version

N/A — CI-level optimization across simulation and hardware jobs.

### Host Platform

Other (please specify): GitHub-hosted Ubuntu/macOS and self-hosted Linux
runners.

### Reproduction

Run the pull request CI on the same commit and record each job's wall time and
the following step groups:

```bash
# Group Actions step durations into:
# setup / install / runtime or kernel build / cache / test / DFX
```

Compare p50 and p90 separately by job, OS, execution path, and anonymous
runner performance tier. Do not combine GitHub-hosted, self-hosted, macOS,
Linux, or different self-hosted tiers into one average.

### Expected Performance

- Reduce the p50 and p90 wall time of the target jobs without splitting them.
- Keep the existing `pre-commit` dependency and test semantics.
- Avoid regressions on slower self-hosted runner tiers.
- Keep representative per-PR coverage and run lower-frequency coverage in
  Daily CI.

### Actual Performance

Recent successful PR CI runs show the following p50 values:

| Job / runner | Job | Install | Scene | DFX |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| a2a3sim / Ubuntu | 10.9m | 2.3m | 6.9m | 1.2m |
| a2a3sim / macOS | 11.2m | 1.8m | 7.0m | 1.4m |
| a5sim / Ubuntu | 10.5m | 2.3m | 6.5m | 59s |
| a5sim / macOS | 10.9m | 2.6m | 6.5m | 1.0m |

Onboard results vary significantly by runner tier: the observed p50 ranges
from 7.4m to 22.7m for a2a3 and from 3.4m to 8.6m for a5.

### Profiling Data (Optional)

Scene execution is about 60% of sim ST wall time, while package installation
usually costs another 1.8-2.6 minutes. Package installation currently invokes
the CMake `ALL` target and can build runtimes that the job does not use.

### Additional Context

Planned work:

- Add coarse step timing for setup, installation, build, cache, test, and DFX.
- Build only the runtime platform required by each CI job and remove repeated
  installation or runtime build work.
- Evaluate remote cache by its total restore/save cost and control job-local
  parallelism by runner tier.
- Re-measure p50 and p90 before changing the per-PR test set.
- If jobs remain slow, retain representative PR smoke coverage and move
  lower-frequency or redundant cases to Daily CI.

Initial test migration candidates:

- Move redundant Collective P4 variants on a2a3sim, a5sim, and a2a3 Onboard
  to Daily CI. Keep all P2 cases, one representative Allreduce Ring P4, and
  the invalid-rank check in PR CI.
- Move the large a5 Onboard `Case1` variants for basic Paged Attention, Batch
  Paged Attention, and Unroll Manual Scope when an equivalent small case is
  already in PR CI.
- Move Benchmark BGEMM, SPMD Paged Attention, 4D Unroll, and similar large
  cases only after adding or promoting an equivalent small PR smoke case.
- Keep Pod, UT, DFX, SDMA, fault recovery, timeout, cross-device dependency,
  and state-machine tests in PR CI because they provide independent or unique
  coverage.

Acceptance criteria:

- No job splitting and no change to the `pre-commit` gate.
- Before/after p50 and p90 are reported for every affected runner path and
  tier.
- Cache changes include hit rate, transfer time, and storage size.
- Every case removed from PR CI records the saved time, retained smoke
  coverage, and its Daily CI destination.

## #1791 [Performance] A2A3 fresh AICore stream per run regresses repeated HCA/SWA Effective latency by 3.8–4.4%

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/issues/1791
- Created: 2026-08-11T13:21:13Z
- Updated: 2026-08-17T07:15:58Z
- Closed: 2026-08-17T07:15:58Z

### Body

## Background

In pypto-lib, repeated same-image DeepSeek-V4 Flash HCA/SWA execution on
`a2a3` with the `tensormap_and_ringbuffer` runtime has a performance
regression at Simpler PR #1540: median `effective_us` increases by 3.81–4.36%.

Repro cases:

- `models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_attention_hca.py`
- `models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_attention_swa.py`

Both entrypoints and their helpers are public at pypto-lib
`1f48761cb5be21a8cf0611fad10d513ba40b0863` on `main`. The test also applies
the public pypto-lib commit `c0751b7582618f7ccef29385236b1964cb480d42`,
which only migrates 17 `valid_shapes` keyword arguments to `valid_shape`.

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
| --- | --- |
| pypto-lib | `1f48761cb5be21a8cf0611fad10d513ba40b0863` + compatibility patch `c0751b7582618f7ccef29385236b1964cb480d42` (`main`) |
| PyPTO | `2e59c01ccc34e586e19b49ecaa1a94b2e21db459` (`main`) |
| Simpler baseline | `8e00319e28cd2ea9f7f7f795a2b1e182956b91bd` (detached) |
| Simpler regressing commit | `e51c3aeecfaf982137b6adc67ca13749b0c95717` (detached) |
| PTOAS | `0.54` |
| PTO ISA | `83d01313d9bfc247c4b7c8bcf969d1019f0d106f` |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |
| Driver / Ascend HAL | `26.0.rc1` / `7.35.23` |
| Python | `3.10.19` |

Controlled A/B note: PyPTO `2e59c01c` records Simpler `dccb8379`. To isolate
PR #1540, the runtime checkout was intentionally overridden with the PR parent
and PR commit above. PTOAS and PTO ISA remained fixed. A separate pin-consistent
PyPTO runtime-bundle A/B independently showed the same regression direction and
magnitude.

Diagnosis: **simpler** — the direct Simpler parent/commit A/B reproduces the
regression while pypto-lib, PyPTO, PTOAS, PTO ISA, model inputs, and benchmark
settings remain fixed.

### Platform

`a2a3 (Ascend 910B/C hardware)`

### Runtime Variant

`tensormap_and_ringbuffer`

### Summary

Simpler PR #1540 changes the A2/A3 runner from retaining an AICore stream for
repeated runs of the same image to creating and retiring a fresh AICore stream
for every run. A direct parent/commit A/B on DeepSeek-V4 Flash HCA and SWA shows
median `effective_us` regressions of 4.36% and 3.81%, respectively.

Each endpoint used 5 warmups followed by 100 measured iterations. All four
runs passed `kv_cache` and `x_out` validation.

### Git Commit ID

`e51c3aeecfaf982137b6adc67ca13749b0c95717`

### CANN Version

`9.0.0`

### Driver Version

`26.0.rc1` (Ascend HAL `7.35.23`)

### Host Platform

`Linux (aarch64)` — Huawei Cloud EulerOS 2.0, kernel
`5.10.0-182.0.0.95.r1941_123.hce2.aarch64`

### Reproduction

Use isolated checkouts and a separate virtual environment for each Simpler
endpoint.

```bash
git -C <pypto-lib-checkout> checkout \
  1f48761cb5be21a8cf0611fad10d513ba40b0863

git -C <pypto-lib-checkout> show --format= \
  c0751b7582618f7ccef29385236b1964cb480d42 \
  -- models/deepseek/v4-flash/hc_pre.py | \
  git -C <pypto-lib-checkout> apply -

git -C <pypto-checkout> checkout \
  2e59c01ccc34e586e19b49ecaa1a94b2e21db459
git -C <pypto-checkout> submodule update --init --recursive

git -C <pypto-checkout>/runtime checkout <runtime-revision>
git -C <pto-isa-checkout> checkout \
  83d01313d9bfc247c4b7c8bcf969d1019f0d106f

source <CANN-root>/set_env.sh
export PTO_ISA_ROOT=<pto-isa-checkout>

python -m pip install --no-build-isolation -e <pypto-checkout>
python -m pip install --no-build-isolation -e <pypto-checkout>/runtime

task-submit --ptoas 0.54 --device 4 --timeout 0 --max-time 1800 --run '
cd <pypto-lib-checkout>
export PYPTO_BENCH=1
export PYPTO_BENCH_WARMUP=5
export PYPTO_BENCH_ROUNDS=100
export PYPTO_BENCH_RAW=1
export PTO2_RING_TASK_WINDOW=262144
export PTO2_RING_DEP_POOL=262144
export PTO2_RING_HEAP=2147483648
export PYPTO_RUNTIME_LOG=error

python models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_attention_hca.py \
  -p a2a3 -d "$TASK_DEVICE" \
  --start-pos 8192 --enable-l2-swimlane 0

python models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_attention_swa.py \
  -p a2a3 -d "$TASK_DEVICE" \
  --start-pos 8192 --enable-l2-swimlane 0
'
```

Run once with baseline runtime
`8e00319e28cd2ea9f7f7f795a2b1e182956b91bd`, then repeat with
`e51c3aeecfaf982137b6adc67ca13749b0c95717`.

### Expected Performance

With parent commit `8e00319e28cd2ea9f7f7f795a2b1e182956b91bd`:

| Case | Median `effective_us` |
| --- | ---: |
| HCA | 259.2 us |
| SWA | 244.0 us |

Repeated same-image execution should retain this steady-state latency after
warmup while preserving correctness when different images alternate.

### Actual Performance

With PR #1540 commit `e51c3aeecfaf982137b6adc67ca13749b0c95717`:

| Case | Median `effective_us` | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| HCA | 270.5 us | +11.3 us / +4.36% |
| SWA | 253.3 us | +9.3 us / +3.81% |

Test window: 2026-08-11 19:05:39–19:10:05 UTC+8. One 100-round batch was
run per endpoint/case. A separate PyPTO runtime-bundle boundary A/B produced
HCA +12.5 us and SWA +8.7 us, independently corroborating the result.

### Profiling Data (Optional)

Before PR #1540, `ensure_run_stream_set(slot, aicore_image_hash)` returns
immediately when the retained AICore stream carries the same image hash. The
5 warmups and 100 measured rounds therefore share one AICore stream.

After PR #1540:

- `RunStreamSlots::acquire()` always creates a fresh AICore stream.
- The stream is retired after every completed run.
- The 5-warmup/100-round benchmark therefore uses 105 fresh AICore streams.

The reported `effective_us` metric is the on-device merged orch/sched window.
Host-side `rtStreamCreate` occurs before that device window, and
`rtStreamDestroy` occurs after device completion and timing readback. The
9–11 us regression is therefore not direct host stream API latency.

Generated AICore binaries are unchanged across the direct A/B:

| Case | Byte-identical child binaries | Regression per child |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| HCA | 35/35 | 0.323 us |
| SWA | 28/28 | 0.332 us |

The strongest current explanation is a device-side cold-start effect: using a
fresh stream for every same-image run prevents retention of prior
instruction-fetch/I-cache/stream-affinity state. The commit boundary and stream
lifecycle change are proven; PMU `icache_req`/`icache_miss` data or a
stream-only toggle is still needed to confirm the exact hardware mechanism.

### Additional Context

The fresh-stream policy was introduced for correctness when different images
are published to the same GM code address. A plain restoration of the old
per-slot image-hash cache may reintroduce stale-instruction risk for an
`A -> B -> A` sequence across depth-two slots.

A safer remediation direction is runner-wide, generation-aware same-image
reuse: reuse only for consecutive identical images when no overlapping code
range has been republished, and recreate the stream when image identity or code
address generation changes. Stable non-overlapping code banks or a supported
AICore instruction-cache invalidation operation are alternatives.

Acceptance should cover repeated same-image performance, alternating-image
correctness, depth-two slot alternation, and stream-creation counts.

Source inspection of Simpler `main` at
`c5a587400721ea98f0a00321569088a5321539b9` shows that
`RunStreamSlots::acquire()` still unconditionally creates a fresh AICore stream.
The numerical A/B above was performed at the PR parent/commit, not at that
latest-main commit.

Related: #1717 discusses hiding per-run device launch latency and persistent
execution for `host_build_graph`; this report concerns repeated same-image
device Effective regression in `tensormap_and_ringbuffer`.
